# CircularProgress accessibility conformance

Rated against WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA. See the [reports legend](../accessibility.md).

| Result                | Count |
| :-------------------- | :---- |
| ✅ Supports           | 8     |
| ⚠️ Partially Supports | 3     |
| ❌ Does Not Support   | 0     |
| ➖ Not Applicable     | 44    |
| 🚩 Flagged            | 5/11  |

## Known gaps

- ⚠️ **1.4.11 Non-text Contrast.** <!-- 1.4.11:gap:start -->With `enableTrackSlot`, a light-mode `warning` arc is about `2.72:1` against its track, below `3:1`. Against the page, every default palette color clears `3:1`.<!-- 1.4.11:gap:end -->
- ⚠️ **2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide.** <!-- 2.2.2:gap:start -->The `indeterminate` variant animates indefinitely with no built-in pause, stop, or hide control.<!-- 2.2.2:gap:end -->
- ⚠️ **4.1.3 Status Messages.** <!-- 4.1.3:gap:start -->The `progressbar` role is not a live region, so `value` changes are not announced unless the surrounding application adds one.<!-- 4.1.3:gap:end -->

## Success criteria

### 🔍 Manual

#### 1.3.3 Sensory Characteristics · A

`✅ Supports` · `○ Author`

<!-- 1.3.3:start -->

- The spinner carries an author-supplied accessible name, so it can be referenced by name rather than only by shape, color, or position.
- Instructions in the surrounding content must not rely on a sensory characteristic alone (for example, "wait for the spinning circle").

**Manual testing steps**

1. Find product copy that tells the user to watch or wait for a circular progress indicator.
2. Check that it names the indicator by its label, not only by color, shape, size, or position.

<!-- 1.3.3:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.3.3:pass:start -->no instruction relies on a sensory characteristic alone.<!-- 1.3.3:pass:end -->

#### 1.4.1 Use of Color · A

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `● Component`

<!-- 1.4.1:start -->

- Determinate progress is conveyed by the length of the arc (`stroke-dashoffset` on the circle) and by `aria-valuenow`, not by color, so the value survives without color. A unit test asserts `value={70}` sets `strokeDashoffset` to `38.076px` on the default circumference.
- The `color` prop (`primary`, `error`, and so on) is decorative and does not encode the value. Whether the arc is visually distinguishable from the page, or from the track when `enableTrackSlot` is set, is a contrast question, covered by 1.4.11.

**Manual testing steps**

1. In a UI with circular indicators of different colors, turn on a grayscale view (in Chrome DevTools: Rendering tab, Emulate vision deficiencies, Achromatopsia).
2. Confirm a determinate arc's length still shows how much is complete.

<!-- 1.4.1:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.4.1:pass:start -->the value can be understood without color.<!-- 1.4.1:pass:end -->

#### 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast · AA

`🚩` · `⚠️ Partially Supports` · `● Component`

<!-- 1.4.11:start -->

- The arc is a `currentColor` stroke. For a named `color`, the root sets that color to `palette[color].main`; `color="inherit"` sets none. By default there is no track, so the adjacent color is the page. With `enableTrackSlot`, a second circle paints the same color at `action.activatedOpacity` (`0.12` in light mode, `0.24` in dark mode) and is `aria-hidden`.
- Measured from the default theme, arc against page (`#fff` light, `#121212` dark):

| Color       | Light vs page | Light vs track | Dark vs page | Dark vs track |
| :---------- | ------------: | -------------: | -----------: | ------------: |
| `primary`   |        4.60:1 |         3.94:1 |      10.71:1 |        6.28:1 |
| `secondary` |        6.30:1 |         5.21:1 |       7.84:1 |        5.08:1 |
| `error`     |        4.98:1 |         4.16:1 |       5.09:1 |        3.86:1 |
| `warning`   |        3.11:1 |         2.72:1 |       9.64:1 |        5.88:1 |
| `info`      |        3.86:1 |         3.33:1 |       8.13:1 |        5.30:1 |
| `success`   |        5.13:1 |         4.36:1 |       7.92:1 |        5.11:1 |

- `color="inherit"` strokes with the parent's CSS `color`, so its contrast depends on where it's used and is the author's responsibility.
- No axe rule checks graphical-object contrast. The 1.4.11 text exception does not apply: a value label in the demos is author-supplied `Typography`, not part of the component.

**Manual testing steps**

1. With a contrast checker (the color picker in browser DevTools shows a ratio), measure a determinate arc's stroke against the page, for each color in use, in light and dark mode.
2. Repeat with `enableTrackSlot`, measuring the arc against the track.
3. Check any custom theme colors the application uses.

<!-- 1.4.11:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.4.11:pass:start -->the arc is at least `3:1` against the page, and against the track when `enableTrackSlot` is set. Every default palette color clears the page. Light-mode `warning` against the track is the known failure, about `2.72:1`.<!-- 1.4.11:pass:end -->

#### 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide · A

`🚩` · `⚠️ Partially Supports` · `◐ Shared`

<!-- 2.2.2:start -->

- The `indeterminate` variant runs two infinite CSS animations (`circularRotateKeyframe` and `circularDashKeyframe`, each `1.4s`) that start automatically and last more than five seconds. The component provides no control to pause, stop, or hide them. `disableShrink` removes the dash animation only; the rotation continues.
- 2.2.2's sufficient techniques call for an in-page control to pause, stop, or hide the motion, or for it to stop within five seconds; the component provides neither. A loader that fills the viewport is exempt because the motion is essential, and a spinner removed once loading finishes avoids the "in parallel with other content" trigger.
- Honoring `prefers-reduced-motion` (via `motion.reducedMotion: 'system'`) sets `animation: none` for users who request it, but that addresses Animation from Interactions (2.3.3, AAA), not 2.2.2; the default `never` does not honor it.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Render an `indeterminate` CircularProgress on a page with other content and leave it for more than five seconds.
2. Look for a way to pause, stop, or hide the motion.
3. Set the OS "reduce motion" preference and confirm whether the animation stops. It stops only when the theme sets `motion.reducedMotion: 'system'` (`'always'` stops it regardless of the OS; the default `'never'` never does).

<!-- 2.2.2:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 2.2.2:pass:start -->the user can pause, stop, or hide the motion, or it stops within five seconds. The component supplies no such control; a full-viewport (essential) loader, or a spinner removed once loading finishes, is what keeps it conformant.<!-- 2.2.2:pass:end -->

#### 2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below Threshold · A

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `● Component`

<!-- 2.3.1:start -->

- The rotation is a smooth `360deg` turn over `1.4s`. The dash grows and shrinks once per the same `1.4s` cycle. Nothing flashes, and nothing repeats three times in one second.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Watch a running `indeterminate` CircularProgress, including with `disableShrink`, for any part that flashes more than three times in any one second.

<!-- 2.3.1:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 2.3.1:pass:start -->no part flashes more than three times per second.<!-- 2.3.1:pass:end -->

#### 3.2.4 Consistent Identification · AA

`✅ Supports` · `○ Author`

<!-- 3.2.4:start -->

- For a given set of props the component produces a stable role and value, the precondition for consistent identification; the name comes from the author.
- Consistency is a cross-page property. Confirm that indicators with the same function share a name and presentation, and that one name is not reused for different functions.

**Manual testing steps**

1. List the circular indicators that serve the same function across the product.
2. Compare their accessible names and variants.

<!-- 3.2.4:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 3.2.4:pass:start -->the same function uses the same name and presentation.<!-- 3.2.4:pass:end -->

#### 4.1.3 Status Messages · AA

`🚩` · `⚠️ Partially Supports` · `◐ Shared`

<!-- 4.1.3:start -->

- `role="progressbar"` is not a live region, so updating `aria-valuenow` is not announced while focus is elsewhere. The component adds no `aria-live` region.
- To announce determinate progress, the surrounding application supplies a polite live region (the W3C `ARIA25` pattern). Announcement is an advisory technique, not an automatic failure, and assistive-technology behavior for progressbar values varies.

**Manual testing steps**

1. With a screen reader running (NVDA with Chrome, or VoiceOver with Safari), start a background task tracked by a `determinate` CircularProgress.
2. Move focus away from it and let the value change.
3. Listen for whether the change is announced.

<!-- 4.1.3:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 4.1.3:pass:start -->the change is announced without the user moving focus to it. It is not by default; add a polite live region in the application to convey it.<!-- 4.1.3:pass:end -->

### 🔁 Hybrid

#### 1.3.1 Info and Relationships · A

`✅ Supports` · `● Component`

<!-- 1.3.1:start -->

- The root sets `role="progressbar"`. The `determinate` variant adds `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, and `aria-valuemax` when a value is supplied; the `indeterminate` variant omits `aria-valuenow`, which WAI-ARIA defines as the correct pattern for an unknown value. The optional track circle is `aria-hidden`.
- axe-core `aria-allowed-attr`, `aria-valid-attr`, `aria-valid-attr-value`, and `aria-roles` pass across the demos in [`progress.a11y.json`](../../../../docs/data/material/components/progress/progress.a11y.json), and unit tests assert the role and value attributes.

**Manual testing steps**

1. In the accessibility tree (in Chrome DevTools: Elements panel, Accessibility tab), inspect a `determinate` and an `indeterminate` CircularProgress.
2. Confirm the determinate spinner exposes a value (now, min, max) and the indeterminate spinner exposes the role with no value.

<!-- 1.3.1:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.3.1:pass:start -->role and value match the variant.<!-- 1.3.1:pass:end -->

#### 2.4.6 Headings and Labels · AA

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

<!-- 2.4.6:start -->

- The accessible name serves as the indicator's label. axe-core `aria-progressbar-name` passes on every enrolled demo, confirming a name is present.
- Whether the name describes the operation ("Uploading photos" against a vague name) is an authoring concern.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Read each CircularProgress accessible name out of context.
2. Ask whether it says what is in progress.

<!-- 2.4.6:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 2.4.6:pass:start -->every name describes its operation.<!-- 2.4.6:pass:end -->

#### 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value · A

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: unit `CircularProgress.test.js` · axe-core `aria-allowed-attr` ✅, `aria-conditional-attr` ✅, `aria-deprecated-role` ✅, `aria-hidden-focus` ✅, `aria-prohibited-attr` ✅, `aria-required-attr` ✅, `aria-roles` ✅, `aria-valid-attr` ✅, `aria-valid-attr-value` ✅, `duplicate-id-aria` ✅, `nested-interactive` ✅

<!-- 4.1.2:start -->

- Role: `role="progressbar"` is always set. Value: `determinate` sets `aria-valuenow`/`aria-valuemin`/`aria-valuemax`; `indeterminate` correctly omits the value. Name: the component emits no name of its own; the author supplies it with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, which the [Accessibility](https://mui.com/material-ui/react-progress/#accessibility) docs require. An author can also pass `aria-valuetext`.
- axe-core's `aria-progressbar-name` (name) and `aria-*` attribute rules (role and value) pass across the demos in [`progress.a11y.json`](../../../../docs/data/material/components/progress/progress.a11y.json), and unit tests assert the role and `aria-valuenow`/`min`/`max`. (axe tags `aria-progressbar-name` `1.1.1` upstream, but a `progressbar`'s name obligation sits with 4.1.2.)
- A bare `<CircularProgress />` has a role but no value and no name. A `determinate` spinner exposes the value but still needs an author-supplied name. Whether a supplied name is meaningful needs an assistive-technology review.

**Manual testing steps**

1. With a screen reader running, move to a named spinner of each variant (`indeterminate` and `determinate`), including one labeled by a visible text label via `aria-labelledby` and one with `enableTrackSlot`.
2. Confirm each spinner announces a name, the determinate one announces a value or percentage, and the indeterminate one announces a busy or indeterminate state. The track stays silent.

<!-- 4.1.2:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 4.1.2:pass:start -->name, role, and value are correct for every variant, and the track is silent.<!-- 4.1.2:pass:end -->

### ⚙️ Automated

#### 1.4.10 Reflow · AA

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: Playwright

<!-- 1.4.10:start -->

- The root is `inline-block` with an explicit width and height (default `40px`, overridable with `size`). It does not impose a minimum page width, so a row of spinners wraps with its container. Overflow at 320 CSS pixels comes from the surrounding layout, such as a non-wrapping row. Covered by a Playwright test at a 320px viewport on `CircularDeterminate`.

<!-- 1.4.10:end -->

## Not applicable

- **1.1.1 Non-text Content (A).** <!-- 1.1.1:start -->The component renders no images or icons; the `progressbar` widget's name, role, and value are covered by 4.1.2, not by a text alternative.<!-- 1.1.1:end -->
- **1.2.1 Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded) (A), 1.2.2 Captions (Prerecorded) (A), 1.2.3 Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded) (A), 1.2.4 Captions (Live) (AA), 1.2.5 Audio Description (Prerecorded) (AA).** No audio or video.
- **1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence (A).** <!-- 1.3.2:start -->A single status element whose circle and optional track are presentational, so there is no multi-part reading order to preserve.<!-- 1.3.2:end -->
- **1.3.4 Orientation (AA).** Sets no orientation lock; a layout concern.
- **1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose (AA).** <!-- 1.3.5:start -->Not an input; collects no user data.<!-- 1.3.5:end -->

- **1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) (AA), 1.4.4 Resize Text (AA), 1.4.5 Images of Text (AA), 1.4.12 Text Spacing (AA).** <!-- 1.4.3,1.4.4,1.4.5,1.4.12:start -->The component renders no text. Value labels shown in the demos are author-supplied and outside the component. On `CircularWithValueLabel`, axe reports `color-contrast` incomplete because the caption sits on the SVG and its background cannot be resolved; that rule is recorded and not asserted.<!-- 1.4.3,1.4.4,1.4.5,1.4.12:end -->
- **1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus (AA).** <!-- 1.4.13:start -->Shows no hover or focus content.<!-- 1.4.13:end -->

- **2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) (A).** <!-- 2.4.4:start -->Renders no link.<!-- 2.4.4:end -->
- **2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) (AA).** <!-- 2.4.11:start -->Not focusable, so its focus cannot be obscured.<!-- 2.4.11:end -->
- **2.5.1 Pointer Gestures (A), 2.5.2 Pointer Cancellation (A), 2.5.3 Label in Name (A), 2.5.4 Motion Actuation (A).** <!-- 2.5.1,2.5.2,2.5.3,2.5.4:start -->Not an interactive target: no pointer gestures, no down-event activation, no visible label text, and no motion actuation.<!-- 2.5.1,2.5.2,2.5.3,2.5.4:end -->

## Level AAA

<!-- level-aaa:start -->

- **2.4.12 Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced), 2.4.13 Focus Appearance.** Not focusable, so there is no focus indicator to obscure or restyle.
- **2.5.7** is Level AA and rated above. **3.3.9 Accessible Authentication (Enhanced)** does not apply: this is not an authentication control.
- **2.3.3 Animation from Interactions.** The `indeterminate` rotation and dash reduce only via `motion.reducedMotion`: `system` follows the OS `prefers-reduced-motion` query and `always` removes the animation unconditionally; the default `never` does not, so OS reduced-motion is not honored by default. `🚩`
- **2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced).** Not an activation target.

<!-- level-aaa:end -->
